messages:
maya: heads up — got a bug report from a user trying to run the sample app on Cloudflare Workers. hitting "Cannot use import statement outside a module" even though package.json has "type: module".
jon: ugh. is this the dual-pkg build where we ship both CJS and ESM and use conditional exports?
sam: probably. Workers require pure ESM bundles, and our package currently resolves to the CJS build for some import paths.
maya: exact repro: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` inside the worker, then runtime throws. Local Node ESM works fine.
alex: can you paste package.json exports?
maya: here: ```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
jon: hmm that looks normal. But Workers (and some bundlers) will follow the `require` fallback if resolution heuristics differ. also some edge runtimes ignore `exports` negotiation and prefer the main field.
sam: we discovered a similar issue before — some edge bundlers don't treat package as ESM unless the `module` or `browser` field is present. Also `types` as a separate export can confuse TS resolution in some setups.
maya: user reported TS server couldn't find types in the worker project, so DX hit both runtime and typing. painful onboarding.
alex: short-term workaround: add an explicit entrypoint "./edge": "./dist/esm/index.js" and tell the sample app to import `@redwood/inference/edge`. Ugly but fast.
jon: long-term we should consider: 1) canonical ESM default in exports (point `.` at esm and provide `require` as a secondary fallback), 2) include a `module` field and `browser` that point to ESM, 3) ensure types are included under the same export path (e.g., "./": { "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts", "import": "..." }).
sam: +1 also add a note in the sample app readme about edge runtimes and the explicit `/edge` import until we roll the fix.
maya: also saw an auth/retry discrepancy: the edge bundle's default retry logic pulls in Node-only timers, causing a crash at runtime. the bundler tree-shakes differently for ESM vs CJS.
alex: -- That is scary. we probably have conditional requires for `node-fetch` vs `fetch` and our retry backoff util uses `setTimeout` polyfill in the ESM build; bundlers sometimes drop the polyfill.
jon: plan: I'll open a PR to make ESM the default export, consolidate types under the same export, and add an explicit `edge` export for immediate relief. sam, can you add a smoke test for Cloudflare/Workers in CI? maya, can you update the sample app's readme and add the workaround snippet?
sam: yes, I'll add a small smoke CI job (runs in emulation) and a failing test to lock the behavior.
maya: will do the readme + sample fix. tagging @dev-bot to create the follow-up tickets.
dev-bot: created issues #4123 (package exports: default to ESM + types consolidation), #4124 (edge smoke CI), #4125 (sample app edge onboarding note) — assigned to jon, sam, maya respectively. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks team. once we ship, let's bake a quick internal doc that lists runtime gotchas for edge (module resolution, timer polyfills, global fetch differences).
jon: agreed. keeping this tiny thread as the canonical quick log for the change. anyone else hit similar?
